1. In Sessions Case No. 35 of 1987 on the file of the IIIrd Additional Sessions Judge, Ernakulam, four accused were tried for offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 323, 326, 302 and 201 IPC. The trail court acquitted A-4 and convicted A-1 under Section 120-B read with Section 302 IPC and also convicted A-2 and A-3 under Sections 302 read with Section 120-B IPC and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life. On appeal, the High Court acquitted A-3 but confirmed the convictions and sentences of A-1, PK. Narayanan and A-2, V.V Salim @ Sasi.
Hence, A-1 has filed Criminal Appeal No. 315 of 1990 and A-2 has filed Criminal Appeal No. 316 of 1990 in this Co
facts: P K. Narayanan v State Of Kerala
No. 315 of 1990 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 30 March 1990 of the Kerala High Court in Cr. A. Nos. 247, 248 and 250 of 1988.) with No. 316 of 1990 and S.L.P. (Cr.) Nos. 3329-31 of 1994
The Judgment was delivered by : K. Jayachandra Reddy, J.
1. In Sessions Case No. 35 of 1987 on the file of the IIIrd Additional Sessions Judge, Ernakulam, four accused were tried for offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 323, 326, 302 and 201 IPC.
issues: Whether the death of Peethambaran is a case of homicide or suicide?

If it is a case of homicide, whether A-2 and A-3 voluntarily caused grievous hurt to Peethambaran by beating with a stick and torch on the terrace of the Polakulath Tourist Home at Palarivattom and then threw or pushed him down to the southern courtyard with the intention to cause his death on 22-4-1983 at about 4.30 a.m.?
Whether A-2 and A-3 caused the death of Peethambaran at the instance and instigation of A-1 and in pursuance of a criminal conspiracy, between A-1 to A-3?
Whether A-4 is privy to the conspiracy to cause the death of Peethambaran?
Whether A-1 to A-4 in pursuance of a criminal conspiracy, tampered with the evidence of murder to screen the offenders from legal punishment and gave false information to the police?
Whether the accused are guilty and if so for what offence?
petitioner_arguments: The plea of the accused has been one of denial.
As stated above ultimately A-1 and A-2 are found guilty.
court_reasoning: So far as point 1 is concerned, the medical evidence assumes lot of importance in this case.
The trial court, however, finally held that the death of deceased was a case of homicide and not suicide.
On point 2 the trial court held that A-2 and A-3 voluntarily caused grievous hurt to the deceased on the terrace and threw him down from the terrace to the southern courtyard at a depth of 65 feet.
On point 3, the trial court held that it was at the instance and instigation of A-1 that A-2 and A-3 caused the death of the deceased in pursuance of a conspiracy among A-1 to A-3.
holding: A-1 guilty under Section 120-B read with Section 302 IPC
A-2 under Section 302 read with Section 120-B IPC
